title: The transistor
summary: Planar, FinFET, gate-all-around and CFET: how the switch keeps shrinking without leaking.

links.why: doping and fields make the switch
billions of switches make up a processor

links.then: each one varies and ages more, so chips need more margin

ideas.how: leakage forced the switch from planar to FinFET to gate-all-around
leaking switches burn power even when they are off
a transistor's current changes smoothly; digital logic uses only on and off

tradeoffs.how: switches that turn on harder also leak more when off

measures.how: billions of switches, each one shrinking
each new node changes the switch's shape

learn.plain: A transistor is a tap for electricity, and the gate is the handle. As taps got tiny, they started dripping even when closed. Each new design grips the pipe from more sides so it shuts off tightly.
learn.engineer: Subthreshold swing is (kT/q)·ln10·(1 + C_dep/C_ox), which has a floor of about 60 mV per decade at room temperature. Short-channel effects appear as drain-induced barrier lowering and threshold roll-off; wrapping the gate around the channel restores electrostatic control so gate length can shrink with acceptable leakage. Nanosheet width can vary by cell to trade drive current for area, and the forksheet adds a dielectric wall between n and p sheets on the way to CFET.

quiz.q: Why did the industry move from planar transistors to FinFETs and nanosheets?
options: To give the gate more control over the channel and cut leakage
To make chips easier to see
quiz.why: Wrapping the gate around more of the channel lets transistors shrink without leaking too much.

quiz.q: In a gate-all-around transistor, the gate touches the channel on…
quiz.why: That is the meaning of gate-all-around. FinFETs touch three sides; planar transistors only the top.

quiz.q: What does a CFET stack on top of each other?
quiz.why: Stacking the complementary pair roughly halves the area of a logic cell.
